column2: Both describe object shapes. Interfaces can be extended and merged; type aliases can also name unions, primitives and tuples. Pick one convention and be consistent.
A union whose members share a literal field (e.g. ok: true | ok: false) that TypeScript uses to narrow the type.
In the default branch, assign the value to a variable of type never: if a new union member is added and not handled, it no longer fits never → compile error.

column1: Why return a Result instead of throwing?
column2: The failure is part of the type, so callers must handle it; exceptions are invisible in signatures and easy to forget.
any switches type checking off. unknown accepts anything but forces you to narrow (check its type) before using it.
Passing a component its collaborators (e.g. a MixerContext) instead of creating them inside, so tests can pass in fakes.
